title: Make a routine map without a weight-loss promise
summary: Organize a habit around a real constraint and review the process without assuming a health outcome.
author: Form editorial source author (AI-assisted)

sections.heading: Choose a process, not a forecast
paragraphs: NIDDK’s habit guidance describes planning for barriers and revisiting a plan. It does not establish a weight outcome from a particular planning worksheet.

Choose a routine you can describe without a scale: preparing a shopping list, organizing a meal break or deciding when an appropriate activity could fit. This is an organizational decision. It is not a calorie prescription, medical treatment or a promise of weight loss.

sections.heading: Draw the chain of decisions
paragraphs: Write the routine in the center of a sheet. To its left, write what has to happen before it can begin. To its right, write what happens afterward. A plan to cook may depend on shopping, storage, available time and someone else’s schedule.

Circle the part you can influence this week. If the main obstacle is transport, a motivational slogan does not solve it. Describe the missing resource so you can decide whether a different routine is more realistic.

sections.heading: Create an obstacle card
paragraphs: Use a separate card for the situation most likely to interrupt the routine. Keep it practical and avoid treating a disruption as a moral failure.
checklist: When this obstacle appears, which decision becomes difficult?
What alternative is available within my resources?
Whose cooperation or advice would I need?
When will I review whether this alternative helped?

sections.heading: Read the record in context
paragraphs: Review what happened to the routine and what made it harder or easier. That observation is useful even if body weight does not change. Do not infer a diagnosis or a treatment response from this worksheet.

Questions about nutrition, weight-related treatment or an activity plan for a medical condition belong with appropriately qualified professionals. This resource helps organize the conversation; it does not replace it.

sources.title: Changing Your Habits for Better Health
sources.supports: Planning around barriers and reviewing habits; no promised weight change from this worksheet.
